title: buy_stamp input
description: §6.3 — buy_stamp(count, payment, holder, provision = false) -> StampReceipt. P-13: no field here carries private-key material, and none ever will; the buyer signs in its own process (§14.2). A release artifact, not a specification schema: §18.5 fixes the fourteen files in spec/schemas/ and the tools' inputs are not among them (T-P15-4).

payment.description: §14.2's two legs, and the two halves of the exchange. Called with no signature, buy_stamp QUOTES: the Postmaster reads the price message current on consensus, builds and freezes the purchase body, and returns it with a reference, having signed nothing. Called again with that reference and the buyer's signature over that body, it SETTLES. The method must be one the Postmaster publishes on its price topic, or STAMP_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED.

network.description: CAIP-2, as the price list names it.

from.description: The account the price is debited from. §6.3 names no buyer because in the ordinary case the holder is the buyer — but it cannot be where the holder is a bare public key, since the account that would pay is the one this purchase creates (§4.6). Absent, the holder pays for itself.

quoteRef.description: The reference the quote came back under. Present on every leg after the quote — the settling call, each carried provisioning body, and the request for the receipt: it names which frozen purchase this answers, and §14.2 requires that a payment reference settle at most one purchase (T-P11-5).

signature.description: The buyer's signature over the body the Postmaster froze, made in the buyer's own process. NOT a transaction: returning a whole signed transaction would make 'never accept a body it did not build' a comparison the Postmaster has to remember to run correctly, where returning a signature makes it structural — the body is the one it froze and stored, and there is no second body for the check to be wrong about (T-P13-3).

publicKey.description: The buyer's PUBLIC half. Never a private key (P-13).

carry.description: One provisioning body, for the Postmaster to decide about and co-sign — §6.1's carry, inside the purchase and nowhere else (D-157, D-168, LIMITATIONS L-5). Present only under a reference whose provisioning purchase is outstanding. The Postmaster reads the body it is being asked to pay for and signs it only if it is a row of the provisioning template for this holder; anything else is refused and no mark is left (§3.5). The body is a TransactionBody the buyer has already signed with its own key: it is public the moment it reaches a consensus node, and there is no field here for a private key and never will be (P-13, T-P13-1).

body.description: The frozen body's bytes, base64 — exactly what the buyer's own signer was handed.

receipt.description: Ask for the receipt of a provisioning purchase. §5.4 names the entities the Postmaster created for the holder, so the receipt is issued only once the Postmaster can read every one of them back from a mirror node AND the holder resolves under §9.2 from its reader. Until then the reference stays outstanding and this returns which rows are still open, which is what makes a purchase interrupted between rows resumable from either side (D-168).

holder.description: §6.3: {account} | {publicKey}. A public key with no account is the leg P-16 names - the transfer creates the account that holds the stamps (§4.6).

publicKey.description: The buyer's PUBLIC half. Never a private key (P-13).

provision.description: §6.3, D-161, D-168 — also provision the holder under §4.6. False unless the Postmaster publishes a provisioning price (§14.3). Where true, the holder must be a bare PUBLIC KEY: the purchase creates the account, and a holder that already has one has nothing left to provision (D-165). The Postmaster then creates the mailbox it sold, paying for each body the agent signs, and the receipt carries the `provisioning` line naming what it created. Provisioning is never required: a holder that brings its own topics leaves this false and the receipt carries no provisioning line.
